rationale: The order is wrong: raw speed falls from about 1.4 to about 0.1 m/s between roughly 52.7 and 53.3 s, before the 66° left turn starts at about 53.5 s (it ends around 55.2 s), and the robot then speeds up, so there is no braking after the turn starts. The smoothed drop from 0.52 to 0.07 after 53.5 s is lag from the 0.9 s filter, not a new brake.

The robot brakes and then turns: braking is essentially done by about 53.3 s, the turn runs from about 53.5 to 55.2 s, and speed then rises from 0.07 to 0.86 m/s by 57 s. No brake of 30% or more follows the start of the turn.

No person is in front at 53.98 s, and a new person with a backpack is in front walking toward the doors at 54.98 s. The robot then speeds up from about 55.2 s: smoothed speed goes from 0.07 at 55.0 s to 0.61 at 56.0 s and 0.78 at 56.5 s, well over 0.3 m/s within 2 s. The episode sits inside [53,57].
